definitions.gloss: a glance, a glimpse, a brief look
definitions.explanation: A quick, brief look at something or someone. Often implies a dismissive or casual glance, or a swift survey of a situation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{書類|しょるい}に{一瞥|いちべつ}をくれた。
examples.english: He gave the documents a quick glance.

examples.japanese: {一瞥|いちべつ}しただけで、{興味|きょうみ}なさそうに{立|た}ち{去|さ}った。
examples.english: After just a glance, she walked away looking uninterested.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}を{一瞥|いちべつ}すると、{何|なに}かが{変|か}わっていることに{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: When I glanced around the room, I noticed something had changed.

notes:
USAGE:
A literary or formal word for a brief look. Often implies that the glance is quick and possibly dismissive. Common in written narrative and formal speech. Can be used with する (to glance) or くれる/{与|あた}える (to give a glance).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一瞥|いちべつ}する (to glance at)
- {一瞥|いちべつ}をくれる (to give a glance)
- {一瞥|いちべつ}もしない (to not even glance at)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ちらっと{見|み}る: to glance — casual, everyday expression
- {一瞥|いちべつ}: a glance — more literary and formal
